title: Community-acquired pneumonia improving on IV levofloxacin

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), case list approved by the owner

story: A 59-year-old man admitted with community-acquired pneumonia is on IV levofloxacin 750 mg daily, hospital day 3. He has been afebrile for 48 hours, eats normally, and his heart rate, respiratory rate and oxygen saturation on room air are normal.

results.text: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count

expected_findings.summary: Clinically stable, afebrile for 48 hours and eating: IV levofloxacin can change to the same dose by mouth.

reference_answer: Change to levofloxacin 750 mg by mouth once daily, completing a 5-day total course if he stays clinically stable.
rationale: Levofloxacin's oral bioavailability is close to complete, so the oral dose matches the IV dose. He meets clinical stability criteria. The stewardship module has nothing to flag: the agent and dose are appropriate.

citations.supports: Clinical stability and total duration of at least 5 days for community-acquired pneumonia; oral therapy once stable.
Stewardship programs promoting timely IV to oral transition once criteria are met.
